author: CNN
description:
The Republican Party’s midterm campaign has turned into a triage operation just three weeks out from November, as officials race to avert losses in a string of once-safe seats that they increasingly fear could cost them total control of Congress. 

The worsening landscape has alarmed GOP operatives across several battleground states, forcing the party to pour resources into traditionally red districts and states at the expense of their once-expansive ambitions in Democratic areas. 

And after months of pressing President Donald Trump to ramp up his travel on behalf of key candidates, some Republicans now worry he’s grown so unpopular that his presence on the campaign trail may in some cases be doing more harm than good. 

CNN’s Lauren Fox reports and CNN’s Dana Bash and Manu Raju break down the GOP anxiety as the campaign calendar shrinks ahead of the midterm elections.

0:00 Is Trump doing more harm than good to GOP candidates on the campaign trail?  
2:44 What is the strategy behind
title: Trump backlash stokes GOP fears of a midterm wipeout

author: CNN
description:
Federal officers executed a search warrant early Monday at the Washington, DC-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota Democrat who has been the persistent target of ire from President Donald Trump’s administration, according to a Justice Department spokesperson and a source familiar with the matter. The congresswoman is running for reelection, and the search warrant was executed only weeks before the midterms.

The Department of Justice said in a statement Monday that investigators from Homeland Security Investigations, a branch of the Department of Homeland Security that handles criminal investigations, “executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice.” “This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” a DOJ spokesperson said.

Omar called the search “the latest escalation” in Trump’s “campaign of political intimidation.”

0:29 CNN correspondent on what we know

title: Feds search Rep. Omar's home; she calls it 'political intimidation'

description:
The Department of Homeland Security and NYC officials remain at odds over immigration agents’ tactics that led to them opening fire on 28-year-old Oscar Belgal. Federal officials accuse Belgal of trying to drive his Honda CRV into agents in the city’s Marble Hill neighborhood in the Bronx during a targeted enforcement operation.

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CNN’s Jake Tapper that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents acted appropriately, in part because New York refuses to honor the agency’s requests to detain undocumented people accused of crimes.

CNN's Priscilla Alvarez also reports on an incident where a man was injured after being struck by an ICE vehicle near Houston, Texas Saturday.

description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia had already violated the surprise energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump over the weekend. 

Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to what he described as an “energy ceasefire,” a development that Zelensky said Kyiv did not know about in advance, and one that Moscow has remained tight-lipped about in the hours since. 

CNN’s Betsy Klein reports on Trump’s surprise ceasefire announcement and his deal with Putin to allow Russian diesel imports in the US. Former NATO commander James Stavridis and Ukrainian Member of Parliament Oleksiy Goncharenko share their reactions.

The kingdom launched a major offensive last week to support Yemeni government forces fighting the Houthis, but the rebels have so far held their ground. 

CNN’s Oren Liebermann has the details. Also, CNN national security analyst Alex Plitsas and Middle East analyst Farea Al-Muslimi discuss Saudi Arabia’s options for responding to the attacks.
